title: TN Social Studies assessment item
$comment: The gates read `required` from this file. One list, so schema and gates cannot drift apart.

choices.$comment: Required for single-select types. Every wrong choice carries its own explanation naming the specific misconception it catches — distractors written to be merely wrong are noise.

misconception.$comment: Null on the key. Required and distinct on every distractor.

correctAnswer.$comment: Must name a choice id that exists.

dokRationale.$comment: The check on the number. A DOK-2 label on a recall stem is the single most common defect and the number alone never reveals it.

standardCodes.$comment: Verbatim from the declared standards file, never typed from memory.

standardsYear.$comment: Pinned. A code is not stable across years.

explanation.$comment: Why the key is right — not a restatement of it.

calibrationStatus.$comment: pre-field-test until real response data exists. Parameters that have never met a student are estimates.

status.$comment: The ITEM's lifecycle. quarantined and unauthored are not servable. Alignment confidence is a separate axis — see alignmentStatus.

alignmentStatus.$comment: Confidence in the item's STANDARD ALIGNMENT — deliberately separate from `status`, which is about the item itself. An item can be perfectly good content whose alignment nobody has verified; collapsing the two axes let an unverified label read as a verdict on the question. evidenced = the item names something that identifies its standard. rehomed = moved on stem evidence, awaiting sign-off. human-verified = a person confirmed it. unverified = KEPT AND USABLE, alignment not established — excluded from standards coverage and from standards-aligned forms, nothing more. not-applicable = the standard names nothing that can be matched.
